name: ticket-to-pr
description: A Jira ticket becomes a validated pull request. The run plans from the ticket (its text and attachments) and your repository, asks you only the questions it cannot reasonably answer itself, then implements in an isolated git worktree and loops — implement, review and QA in parallel, decide — until the change is ready to ship (up to three passes). QA exercises the change the way a user would, not by reading files. You approve before anything leaves the machine; the PR opens from the run's branch (a draft listing what is outstanding if three passes were not enough).

vars.answers: (No blocking questions were raised — proceed on the brief's stated assumptions.)
vars.verdict: (First pass — there is no review feedback yet.)

inputs.name: ticket
inputs.description: The work to do, in whatever form you have it: a Jira key or link (the issue, its attachments and a link are fetched through the Atlassian connection), a GitHub issue link, any other link, or just a description typed here.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.description: The repository the change lands in: a local path, or its URL (a local clone is found, or the Run dialog offers to clone it). The run works in its own worktree on a fresh branch, never in your checkout.

phases.name: plan
phases.description: Turns the ticket into a working brief: goal, checkable acceptance criteria, the assumptions it made, and only the questions that truly block.
phases.prompt:
You are planning the work for this ticket. Your working directory, ${worktrees.repo.path}, is a fresh git worktree of the repository it lands in.

${ticket}

The ticket above is complete — do not look it up again. Read it, look at every attachment it lists, and look at the repository (its structure, conventions, any README or CLAUDE.md). Then write a working brief for the engineer:

## Goal
One or two sentences.

## Acceptance criteria
A numbered list. Each one must be checkable by looking at or running the result.

## Assumptions
The decisions you made where the ticket is silent. Make the sensible call a good engineer would make (stack, file layout, styling, placeholder vs. real content) and say what you chose. Do not ask about these.

## Questions
Only questions where a wrong guess would mean redoing the work, and that neither the ticket nor the repository answers. Usually there are none — write "None." then.

End with exactly one line: `NEEDS-ANSWERS: yes` if you listed a blocking question, otherwise `NEEDS-ANSWERS: no`.

phases.name: needs-answers
phases.description: Reads the brief's last line: is a person needed before building?

phases.name: answers
phases.description: Only when the brief raised blocking questions: the run waits for you, and your approval note is the answer.

phases.name: build
phases.description: Implement, check, decide — repeated until the decision is SHIP, at most three passes. Each pass fixes what the previous one's checks found.

phases.name: implement
phases.prompt:
Implement this ticket in your working directory, ${worktrees.repo.path} — a git worktree of the repository, on branch ${worktrees.repo.branch}. Every file you create goes under that directory: use paths relative to it, or absolute paths that start with it.

${ticket}

Working brief:

${brief}

Answers from the person (these override the brief's assumptions):

${answers}

Feedback from the previous pass (fix every item it lists; ignore this on the first pass):

${verdict}

Rules:
- Meet every acceptance criterion in the brief. Use the ticket's attachments where the ticket refers to them — copy them into the repository; do not substitute a drawing or placeholder for a file you were given.
- Write real content, not lorem ipsum, unless the brief's assumptions say otherwise.
- Before you commit, validate the result the way its user would experience it: run the tests or the build; for a web page, serve it locally, load it in a headless browser, take a screenshot and look at it (Read the image). Fix what looks wrong. To serve a page, start the server so you can stop exactly it: `python3 -m http.server <port> >/dev/null 2>&1 & SERVER_PID=$!` and later `kill $SERVER_PID`. Never stop processes by port (`lsof -ti:<port> | xargs kill` and the like) — that also matches your own process and ends your session.
- Delete what you created only to validate (screenshots, logs, tool output folders) — it never goes in the commit.
- Commit on ${worktrees.repo.branch} with a message that starts with the ticket key.

Return: what you changed (files), how you validated it (commands and what you saw), and anything you could not do.

onError.name: implement-ask
onError.description: Only if implementing fails: the run stops and shows you why; your approval note is guidance, and it tries again.

parallel.name: review
qa

onError.name: qa-ask
onError.description: Only if QA itself fails to run: the run stops and shows you why; your approval note is guidance, and QA runs again.

phases.name: decide
phases.prompt:
Decide whether this change is ready to ship.

Working brief:

${brief}

Review:

${reviewNotes}

QA:

${qaNotes}

SHIP when every acceptance criterion has observed evidence and no blocking or should-fix finding is left. Nice-to-haves never block. Do not block on information the ticket does not provide when the brief made a reasonable assumption.

If the QA report is missing or says QA could not run, that is not something another implementation pass can fix: decide on the review and the engineer's own validation evidence, and say plainly that independent QA did not run.

Otherwise FIX: give a numbered list of the exact changes the engineer must make next pass — each one concrete enough to act on without a follow-up question.

End with exactly one line: `DECISION: SHIP` or `DECISION: FIX`.

phases.name: open-pr
phases.description: Waits for your approval — you see the final decision first — then opens the PR. The first step with an effect outside this run.

onError.name: open-pr-ask
onError.description: Only if opening the PR fails (a rejected push, an auth problem): the run stops and shows you why; your approval note is guidance, and it tries again.
